   "Investors are concerned about potential interest rate caps and late fee restrictions following the midterms, specifically regarding a Democrat-led Congress revisiting these issues.",
   "Card issuer loan yields currently average 27% on a core basis, meaning interest rate caps would exert significant pressure on profitability and likely restrict credit supply to the real economy.",
   "GS modeled three interest rate cap scenarios: 10%, 18%, and 36%. The 10% and 18% caps would cause significant EPS headwinds and large credit supply restrictions.",
   "A 36% interest rate cap on balances yielding above 36% is estimated to have a minimal EPS impact (1-5% across issuers).",
   "Late fee reduction scenarios (20%, 35%, 50%) were modeled, with a 35% reduction resulting in an average 9% EPS headwind for the four main card issuers.",
   "BFH and SYF are identified as having the largest exposure to both interest rate cap and late fee reduction scenarios, while AXP has the least exposure.",
   "Industry pushback is expected to be significant for any legislative changes, similar to the successful legal challenge that vacated the CFPB's prior $8 late fee rule.",
   "Issuers would likely employ mitigants such as credit tightening, reducing marketing, and applying account fees to offset potential revenue losses from regulatory changes."
